risks: Large prospective capacity and contracted-revenue figures require substantial capital deployment and successful site delivery.
Q2 CapEx was $797.5M and GAAP net loss was $1.16B, although the loss was primarily driven by warrant fair-value changes; execution is capital intensive.
Successor bottlenecks shift from power access to construction, cooling/electrical equipment, financing and customer credit as capacity scales.
High customer concentration can transmit counterparty stress directly into liquidity and cash flow.
Large prospective capacity/revenue figures should not be treated as equivalent to delivered capacity or realized economics.
Secured debt and external financing increase fixed obligations while expansion remains construction-intensive.
unknowns: Economics of the full prospective 2.5 GW beyond the anchored 530 MW are not yet contracted or proven.
Future financing cost, customer concentration, build timing and stabilized return on invested capital remain unverified.
Stabilized returns and economics for capacity beyond contracted/anchored deployments remain unproven.
Future customer diversification, financing cost and stabilized ROIC remain unverified.
contradictions: Rapid colocation revenue and capacity growth coexist with very high capital intensity and a large GAAP net loss.
Rapid colocation growth and improving gross profit coexist with unusually high capital requirements and concentrated customer exposure.
